transcript: Well, a couple different things. First of all, this was bipartisan legislation that we passed in the House. We had plenty of hearings on it over the last couple of years as well. But it does a number of things. First of all, we want to know what is the safe law? You know, we're operating on 70 parts per trillion, but should it be 30? should be 100. What is the proper standard? So we require the EPA to tell us, you know, use science, tell us what that standard should be. But this bill also provided grants to cities. You've got cities large and small. What can we do as a federal government to try and help communities that would have to deal with this issue. Now, we did a small piece of this actually on the defense authorization bill that President Trump signed in the law last month, not because we had a provision that again was bipartisan and it went through the conference, the conference committee, but it requires that military installations, when the state has a standard, Michigan is one of those, but if the state has the standard and if it's a military installation caused by the firefighting farm, the Department of Defense is now required to help clean up those sites. So this bill that we passed this week, it's an important step forward. Again, it was bipartisan and I think we'll do a lot of, particularly if we can get it enacted to help the nation deal with this issue.
